historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth, bracketed by the through-cycle FY2009-FY2026 revenue CAGR (4.3%) and the FY2016-FY2026 CAGR (2.9%); the equity CAGR is negative (impairments of $1.3B in FY2025, dividends and the DECIEM buyout exceeding earnings) and the EPS CAGR runs trough-to-trough, so neither is a usable growth anchor.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-9% to -12%) diverges by far more than 30% from the revenue CAGR (-1.5% to -1.8%) and the EPS CAGR (-42%): FY2023-FY2026 span a goodwill/intangible impairment cycle, a $745M NCI buyout and restructuring charges, so all three trailing CAGRs measure the downturn rather than the franchise. Owner FCF (FY2021 ~$2,657M -> FY2023 $330M -> FY2026 $916M) is equally cyclical; the 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (+40%) exceeds the reported-FCF CAGR (+22%) only because the trough base is lower, not because SBC is shrinking (SBC was flat at 2.0-2.2% of revenue).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2021 2,994-327-~10 = ~2,657; FY2023 728-267-131 = 330; FY2024 1,441-325-167 = 949; FY2025 670-304-114 = 252; FY2026 1,316-310-90 = 916. SBC has held at 2.0-2.2% of revenue throughout the downturn, so the owner adjustment does not change the growth picture; the cycle does.

scenario_narratives.base: EL completes the Profit Recovery and Growth Plan (final ~10,000 net position reductions, $1.75B of charges) and Beauty Reimagined restores pre-COVID profitability over five years rather than two: pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 18.6% adjusted in FY2026 to 21% by FY2032, with FY2027 absorbing the ~$310M PRGP tail and tariff costs. Revenue grows 5% in FY2027 on the Q1 run-rate (+6% cc) then fades to 2.5%, averaging 3.5% — below the global prestige-beauty market because the two engines that drove FY2019-22 (mainland China and Asia travel retail, 2,741 and ~900M of FY2026 sales respectively) stabilise but do not re-accelerate, and because makeup (MAC, Too Faced, Smashbox; segment operating income negative in FY2025-26) stays a drag while skin care (FY2026 segment OI $1,416M) and fragrance (+12% in FY2026, +19% in Q1 FY2027) carry the recovery. The cash tax rate normalises from 36% to 25% as US losses stop going unbenefited. The dividend ($508M) is covered by FY2028.
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround lands at FY2022 economics: skin care regains share in China and the US (La Mer, Estée Lauder brand relaunches, The Ordinary scaling), Asia travel retail recovers with the new Beijing/Shanghai airport operators and Hainan, fragrance continues compounding at double digits, and PRGP procurement and supply-chain savings fall through to a 23% pre-SBC EBITDA margin (~17% EBIT) by FY2032. Revenue grows 7% in FY2027 and averages ~4.8% over the decade. IEEPA tariff refunds and benign trade policy remove the FY2027 profitability headwind management flagged. Even here the terminal multiple is capped at 18x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: Beauty Reimagined stabilises but does not re-rate the business: China's prestige consumer stays weak, the duty-free operator change at Beijing and Shanghai airports and Middle East conflict keep travel retail (~2% of sales exposed to the latter) shrinking, Western prestige share continues to leak to indie, dermo and TikTok-native brands, and tariffs on US imports persist. PRGP savings are reinvested in consumer-facing spend just to hold revenue flat-to-2%. Margins settle at ~18% pre-SBC EBITDA — today's adjusted level — the tax rate stays near 30% on a US loss position, and restructuring recurs. No distress: EL remains investment grade with ample liquidity, so the bear case is a value trap, not a solvency event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A trough-recovery valuation, deliberately anchored to neither extreme: the FY2025 reported loss (operating margin -5.5%, $1.3B of impairments) is not extrapolated, and neither is the FY2022 China-fuelled peak (17.9% operating margin, $7.24 adjusted EPS). The base case is a return to EL's own FY2015-19 profitability by FY2032 at growth below the prestige-beauty market; the bull case is a sustained FY2022; the bear case is today's adjusted margin with no growth. All three use the same 8.5% USD WACC so cyclical and execution risk is charged once, in the flows and weights. SBC ($310M, 2.1% of sales) is expensed and the 366.1M diluted count is held flat; operating leases are treated as operating cost and excluded from net debt; the $197M Forest Essentials payment made after the balance-sheet date is deducted in the bridge. At $110 the shares trade at ~44x FY2026 adjusted EPS and ~16x pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA, so the market is already paying for something close to the bull-case recovery at a staples-like discount rate; the gap between that price and the probability-weighted value is the price of the turnaround thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of terminal pre-SBC EBITDA margin is roughly $5-6/share; the base 21% assumes PRGP delivers pre-COVID profitability, which EL has not shown since FY2022.
Mainland China (20% of FY2026 sales, $373M segment OI) and Asia travel retail: a renewed downturn or further duty-free operator disruption drives the bear path; a sharp recovery drives the bull.
Tariffs: management expects an adverse and possibly material effect on FY2027 profitability; IEEPA refund recoveries are an offset of uncertain size.

Restructuring recurrence: $314M of approved PRGP charges remain to be recorded and FY2026 accruals (+$483M other accrued liabilities) unwind in cash in FY2027; a further programme after FY2027 would breach the 0.5pp ongoing allowance.
Tax: a 35.7% adjusted ETR normalising to 25% is worth ~$8-10/share; if US losses persist the rate stays near 30% (bear path).

Discount rate: at 7.5% WACC the base case rises toward the current price; the valuation's distance from the market is largely a disagreement about the required return on a turnaround, not about FY2027 earnings.
Working-capital sign: growth consumes ~10% of incremental revenue; a faster recovery is therefore partly self-funding in the opposite direction from a subscription business.

Intangible impairment: the TOM FORD trademark ($1.8B carrying) had only 19% headroom at April 2026 and is sensitive to a 140bp WACC move — a non-cash risk to book value, not to the DCF, but a signal about brand momentum.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 66.22-121.64
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL core_metrics (106 periods) via make dcf-context; FY2026 10-K (EL_Annual_FY2026.txt: income statement 4140-4160, non-GAAP reconciliation 4540-4567, cash flow 5360-5407, balance sheet 5280-5320, PRGP note 6025-6118, EPS note 7639-7673, lease note 5921-5936); Q1 FY2027 10-Q (EL_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt: statements 1355-1480, debt table 2896-2947, non-GAAP reconciliation 2838-2851, Forest Essentials subsequent event 2460-2474).
data_sources.qualitative: 10-K Outlook and PRGP sections (EL_Annual_FY2026.txt:4225-4272), 10-Q MD&A on tariffs and the Restructuring Program, segment revenue and operating income kpis by product category and region. No EL_Analysis.json existed at build time; scenario axes are drawn from the filings and the segment kpis.

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q, EPS note: 366.1M; basic 363.3M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. 8.0M options were anti-dilutive at FY2026 and are excluded. Note the flat count is a modelling convention EL is not currently funding: buybacks were $70M in FY2026 against $310M of SBC and the diluted count rose from 360.1M (FY2025) to 366.1M.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, 'Non-cash stock-based compensation' $310M (EL_Annual_FY2026.txt:5368). EL publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure; withholding on net-share settlement is netted inside the +$53M 'Net proceeds from stock-based compensation transactions' financing line and is not separately disclosed, so the cash-flow add-back is used as the charge and the $53M proceeds are NOT added to FCF.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (NYSE); Sunday build, no after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.15 x ERP ~4.75% = cost of equity ~9.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (A-/A3 senior notes, 2027-2053 ladder, projected FY2027 interest $290M on $7.1B principal), ~3.4% after tax; market weights ~85/15 at $110 (equity $40.3B, debt $7.25B) give ~8.75%, rounded down to 8.5% to reflect a consumer-staples long-run beta nearer 1.0. The SAME 8.5% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, China/travel-retail and turnaround-execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: US GAAP operating lease cost ($520M FY2026, 10-K lease note line 5929) is expensed inside SG&A and therefore already inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities ($392M current + $1,557M non-current at 2026-09-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial. No separate lease_cost_pct_path is needed because the charge is already in EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required. The DECIEM redeemable NCI was bought out in FY2024 ($745M) and FY2025 ($21M); FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 show no NCI line on the income statement or balance sheet. Flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.restructuring_treatment: PRGP: $1,748M of charges approved, $1,434M recorded through 2026-06-30 (10-K lines 6033/6106), so ~$314M remains to be recorded in FY2027 on top of the cash unwind of FY2026 accruals (other accrued liabilities rose $483M in FY2026). Charges have been recurring at EL (FY2024 $122M, FY2025 $481M, FY2026 $823M; Leading Beauty Forward ran FY2016-21), so they are modelled as a margin drag rather than excluded: -2.0pp of revenue in FY2027, -0.5pp in FY2028, and a mature pre-SBC EBITDA margin of 21% that sits ~0.5pp under the pre-COVID adjusted norm as an ongoing allowance.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: EL is net-debt ($4.05B), so the strict net-cash trigger for stripping interest income is not met; it is deducted anyway because the $3.2B cash is netted against debt in the bridge (matching-asset rule) and because the component build starts from operating income, which excludes it. last_fcf = 1316 - 310 - 90 = 916. Note last_fcf is a levered, trough-ish figure: FY2026 reported FCF is after $331M cash interest and several hundred million of cash restructuring; the projections are unlevered component builds and are not anchored to it.
inputs.guidance_note: No FY2027 guidance figures are in the Extracted/ filings (the 10-K Outlook and 10-Q MD&A are qualitative; the August 2026 earnings 8-K is not in the folder). Year-1 drivers are anchored to the observed run-rate instead: Q1 FY2027 net sales +6% constant currency (+7% reported) and adjusted operating margin 12.1% (449/3,715) vs 7.3% a year earlier; management states tariffs will have an adverse effect on FY2027 profitability. If the 8-K guidance is later added, the FY2027 growth and margin entries are the only drivers that should move.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 2: operating company, consumer, cyclical) with the adaptations file applied for leases, NCI, matching-asset and charge-risk-once. First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF. BASE YEAR: FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) is a recovery-from-trough year, not a mid-cycle year: reported operating income $780M (5.2%) includes $823M PRGP charges and an $84M securities-litigation settlement; adjusted operating income $1,687M (11.2%); pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA 1,687 + 796 D&A + 310 SBC = $2,793M (18.6%). Pre-COVID FY2015-19 pre-SBC EBITDA margins were ~20-21% (operating margins 14.3-15.6%), the FY2022 China/travel-retail peak was 23.8% (17.9%), FY2025 reported was 0.3%. The base case therefore recovers to the pre-COVID norm (21% EBITDA / ~14.9% EBIT by FY2032), NOT to the FY2022 peak, which is reserved for the bull case; the bear case holds roughly today's adjusted margin. Neither the FY2025 trough nor the FY2022 peak is extrapolated. TERMINAL: Gordon binds in base (17.1x) and bear (15.7x vs 16x cap); the 18x cap binds in bull. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables 1,518 + inventory 1,999 - payables 1,578 = $1,939M (12.9% of sales) so growth consumes cash; capture set at -10% of the revenue change. EQUITY BRIDGE: -$197M for the Forest Essentials 51% purchase ($160M) and inducement payment ($37M) paid 2026-10-05 from cash, after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet; the consolidated brand's cash flows are not separately added to the projections, which is slightly conservative (~$0.5/share). Debt is carried at the 10-Q carrying value ($7,251M incl. ~$175M of fair-value swap losses; principal ~$7,100M), also slightly conservative.

bear.rationale: The PRGP savings are reinvested or competed away and EL settles at roughly today's adjusted profitability: 18% pre-SBC EBITDA = ~11.7% EBIT margin vs 11.2% adjusted in FY2026. Growth stalls at 1-2% as China mainland and Asia travel retail do not recover, tariffs stick and US prestige share keeps leaking to indie and dermo brands; the tax rate stays elevated because US earnings stay thin. Cap 16x for a structurally slower business; Gordon at 8.5%/2.0% is 15.7x and binds. No solvency element: A-/A3 rating, $3.2B cash, no maturity above $700M in any year.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +5% (Q1 ran +6% cc on an easy comp; Forest Essentials consolidation adds ~0.5pp; tariffs and a weak Western consumer cap it), fading to 2.5% by FY2035. Ten-year average 3.5%, between the FY2016-26 CAGR of 2.9% and the through-cycle 4.3%; below the ~4-5% global prestige-beauty market because EL has been a share loser in the US and China since FY2022.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA, net of restructuring cash. FY2027 17.5% = ~19.5% adjusted (FY2026 18.6% + ~1pp PRGP savings; Q1 FY2027 adjusted op margin was already 12.1% vs 7.3%) less ~2pp (~$310M) PRGP tail; FY2028 19.3% = 19.8% less 0.5pp; then a glide to 21.0% by FY2032 = the FY2015-19 norm, i.e. a ~14.9% EBIT margin after SBC and D&A, ~0.5pp under pre-COVID as an allowance for the recurring 'one-off' charges EL has booked in 10 of the last 11 years.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted ETR was 35.7% in FY2026 and 38.8% in FY2025 because US losses are unbenefited after the FY2025 valuation allowance and the earnings mix is skewed to higher-tax jurisdictions; as US profitability returns the rate falls toward ~25%, above the ~20-22% of FY2019-22 because of Pillar Two (15% minimum in Switzerland/Belgium) and a higher US share of profit.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 3.0% of sales in FY2026 is a PRGP low (FY2025 4.2%, FY2022-24 5.9-6.3% during the Japan plant and IT builds, FY2018-19 4.6-5.0%); normalised to 4.0% from FY2029. D&A 5.3% in FY2026 includes acquired-intangible amortisation; glides to 4.3%, 0.3pp above capex for the non-replacing intangible amortisation (TOM FORD trademark $1.8B, Too Faced, Dr.Jart+).

bull.rationale: Full recovery to the FY2022 peak economics, sustained: 23% pre-SBC EBITDA = ~16.9% EBIT margin vs 17.9% in FY2022. Growth at or above the prestige-beauty market as skin care (La Mer, Estée Lauder, The Ordinary) regains share in China and the US and fragrance (Le Labo, Jo Malone, TOM FORD, Kilian) keeps compounding double-digit. Gordon at 8.5%/3.0% is 18.7x so the 18x cap binds. Same WACC as base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the thesis rests on a multi-year turnaround under a CEO in place since January 2025, with the two FY2019-22 growth engines (mainland China, Asia travel retail) still structurally impaired, tariffs explicitly flagged by management as an FY2027 profit headwind, and restructuring charges recurring in 10 of the last 11 fiscal years — but not higher, because there is no solvency or covenant element (A-/A3, $3.2B cash, laddered maturities). Bull cut to 25% because it requires several independent things to go right at once: a China prestige recovery, US share stabilisation, PRGP savings fully falling through to a FY2022-like margin, and benign trade policy.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
